clues.label: A musical characteristic
clues.text: Twenty-four songs, all poems by Wilhelm Müller. A man who's been turned down walks out into winter and just keeps going.

clues.label: Places the composer lived and worked
clues.text: Almost his whole short life happened in and around one imperial capital. He often didn't even have his own piano — he crashed with friends.

clues.label: A biographical detail
clues.text: More than six hundred songs for voice and piano. Almost none of his orchestral music got a public performance while he was alive.

clues.label: A relationship with contemporaries
clues.text: His friends ran regular evening hangouts that were just his music, start to finish. People still use the name they coined for those nights.

clues.label: An anecdote
clues.text: Six hundred songs. Dead at thirty-one. And he left a symphony that just... stops after two movements. People still call it the Unfinished. He asked to be buried next to the older deaf master whose funeral he'd walked in as a torchbearer.

explanation.summary: The huge song output, the circle of friends, and Müller's winter wanderer: Franz Schubert, writing in Austria in 1827.

points.text: Twenty-four Müller poems about a winter journey — that's Winterreise, D. 911.
The capital is Vienna. Schubert barely left it, and he wrote this cycle there the year before he died.
Six hundred-odd lieder, almost no public orchestral performances. That imbalance is Schubert's career in one line.
The Unfinished Symphony, death at thirty-one, buried beside Beethoven. Schubert was a torchbearer at that funeral in March 1827 and followed him in November 1828.
